title: Knowledge
tagline: Pramana — the light of true understanding
description: Explore the nature of true knowledge and learn to discriminate between the real and the unreal through sutras on wisdom and discernment.

sutra.meaning: Knowledge comes from i) direct perception, ii) inference or deduction,iii) scriptural testimony.

sections.insight: Direct experience is most powerful. To be in meditation one should decide not to dwell on any logic or be interested in any proof.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I feel a need to be correct or logical all the time? Am I judgemental?
sections.practice:
Observe thoughts without reacting
Do I rely on experience or assumption?
sections.meditation:
3 min Reflection
Observe - how do I form  my opinions. 10 min meditation

sutra.meaning: Wrong or perverse knowledge is false understanding based on what is not a fact or real.

sections.insight: Many beliefs are based on incomplete perception. For instance a person suffering inferiority complex may find others behavior arrogant.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Which of my beliefs may be wrong?
sections.practice: Question one of your assumptions today. Think deeply.
sections.gurudevInsight: Viparyaya :- Patanjali very beautifully described each of these modulations. Pramana is the knowledge that the mind is constantly engaged in arguments, in proofs, in knowledge, analyzing or wrong knowledge, wrong understanding. This moment there could be arguing, proving there could sbe logic in your mind, looking for a proof or it will have a wrong understanding. You will think things the way they are not. Most of the time you impose your own views & ideas & feelings on others and you think that is how they are not. Most of the time you impose your own views & ideas & feelings on others and you think that is how they are.

sutra.meaning: Imagination is based on mere words not based on reality

sections.insight: The mind creates stories without facts. Sometimes its mere pleasureable fantasy but at other times it could be baseless fears.
sections.reflectionPrompt: What story did my mind create?

sutra.meaning: Sleep is a mental state based on absence of thought or knowledge.

sections.insight: When the mind is not seeking proof or deluding or making up stories, it is asleep.
sections.journalPrompt: How does rest or lack thereof affect me?
sections.gurudevInsight: And when you are in waking state, you are constantly engaging in the activities of the senses. Or else you go back to sleep or to dreaming state where you are completely shut off. In sleep & dreaming, same memories come but you are never to your Self- calm, quiet. Uniting all the loose ends of your existence. You become the object of your perception. You know, if you see villagers, or very innocent people or even children when they watch a movie, they are so totally involved in the movie, isn’t it?

sutra.sanskrit:
तत्र निरतिशयं सर्वज्ञबीजम्
स पूर्वेषामपि गुरुः कालेनानवच्छेदात
sutra.meaning:
In Ishvara lies infinite knowledge
The divine is the eternal teacher

sections.insight:
The source of knowledge is within.
Wisdom is timeless.
sections.shlokaFrom: श्रद्धावाँल्लभते ज्ञानं तत्परः संयतेन्द्रियः।ज्ञानं लब्ध्वा परां शान्तिमचिरेणाधिगच्छति॥ 4.39
sections.wisdomFrom: The man of faith obtains knowledge. Devoted to it and controlling his senses, having obtained knowledge he quickly attains supreme peace.
sections.gurudevInsight: When a boundary collapses to the center, what happens? Our little chattering mind, when it prays, it prays to the infinite Being that you are. For that you can say – Ok lord, my lord help. Whomsoever you pray, whatever, wherever you pray and whenever you pray it all reaches me & me alone This is what Krishna says in Gita also, to whomsoever you pray, everything comes to me alone because I am the core of the existence. You may worship that, you may worship this, you may worship something else, means what? Wherever you worship, worship is just an act of dissolving.

sutra.sanskrit: वितर्का हिंसादयः कृतकारितानुमोदिता लोभक्रोधमोहपूर्वका मृदुमध्याधिमात्रा दुःखाज्ञानानन्तफला इति प्रतिपक्षभावनम्
sutra.meaning: Negative thoughts (like violence) caused by greed, anger or delusion—whether done, caused, or approved of, and whether mild, moderate, or intense—result in endless pain and ignorance. Cultivating the opposite, ie., positive thought is necessary to stop this cycle.

sections.insight: One has to develop and exercise the discriminatory faculty to curtail vitarka or dubious, wavering or uncertain knowledge.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I easily believe everything I see or hear or do I take an objective and rational view of things.
sections.practice: Today observe your mind while reading or watching or hearing anything which makes you angry or sad.
sections.journalPrompt: Do I feel immediate emotional reaction within me at every negative info.
sections.gurudevInsight: Or you approve that, approve someone else action. These three comes from greed, anger, and delusion. When you are greedy you make someone else do the action, which you want to do. It’s out of greed, violence or untruth or & all these negative principles thrive. When a person is greedy, he doesn’t see things as they are, also when a person is angry, obsessed with anger, person’s discrimination, mind gets clouded, discrimination disappear, he doesn’t know what he does. So when you are acting or approving some action, see behind that, it is the anger, which is making you do this job?
